§6.6 Printed Page Numbers

📄 Page rule — applied from the page alone

layout-printed-page-numbers · rule layout

✅ Normative

A printed page number (the folio) MUST be kept in the header or footer band it is printed in, verbatim, and MUST NOT appear as a loose element in the body. When the printed page number is requested, it MUST also be recorded on its own for the page, as printed, and MUST NOT be inferred for a page that prints none.

The folio is the number a document prints on itself: 26, Page 6, Page 3 of 12, iv, A-3. It sits in the top or bottom margin, often beside a date, a form number or a URL.

FORM CMS-2567  Previous Versions Obsolete       If continuation sheet Page 3 of 12
                                                                      ↑ the folio

Two records

Record Requirement
In the band The folio is part of the header or footer it is printed in. The band MUST be kept together and verbatim — see Recurring Page Furniture§4.6.
On its own When the printed page number is requested (Output Options§3.5), the number MUST also be recorded alone for the page — the sidecar's printedPageNumber, see The Sidecar§3.4. The label MUST be stripped and the numbering kept as printed: 6, not Page 6; roman numerals stay roman; A-3 stays A-3.

The offset is the point

Front matter, covers and inserts mean printed page 1 is often not sheet 1. A magazine feature can open on sheet 1 and print 26; a report can run twelve sheets of front matter before printing 1. That mapping is a fact about the document, not the page, and it is the reason the number is worth recording separately — a reader citing "page 26" cannot otherwise be sent to the right sheet.

  • The recorded number MUST be the number the page prints. It MUST NOT be renumbered to match the sheet position.
  • A folio MUST NOT be inferred for a page that prints none.

Pages that print nothing

Covers, plates and continuation sheets frequently carry no folio; their printed page number is empty, which is not an error. A pre-printed blank, Page ___ of ___, is also no folio: the blank MUST be transcribed in the band (as [blank]) and no number recorded.

A folio never sits in the body

A number that ends up as a loose line among the page's content means the band was read wrongly. The folio MUST belong to its margin band whether or not the rest of that band was recognised — the same never invent failure as promoting furniture to a heading.
